title: PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) Training Note: Payment Lag and Alert Warning Days
content:
**Rule.** For the reset of a PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) low-balance alert amount, where the latest payment to the enrollment was made by office check and at least 2 payments in the one-month window were made that way, the warning days are increased by 2; where the latest payment was made in cash at an office or at a payment kiosk and at least 2 payments in the one-month window were made those ways, the warning days are increased by 1; with any other payment record they are not increased for payment lag.

The payments are the payments to the enrollment on its PrePay ledger, with their channels and posting dates. A window of a stated number of months takes the records dated after the same day of the month that many months before the current date, through the current date.

### Questions answered

**Latest payment by office check, and one other office check in the window.** Two office-check payments, the latest among them: increased by 2.

**Latest payment at a payment kiosk, one cash payment at an office earlier in the window.** Cash at an office and kiosk payments count together: two of them, the latest among them, so increased by 1.

**Latest payment by office check, the only other payment in the window at a kiosk.** Only one office-check payment lies in the window and the latest is not a cash or kiosk payment: not increased for payment lag.

**Latest payment online by card after three office checks.** The latest payment is neither group: not increased for payment lag.

**Does a mailed check count as an office check?** No. The rule names payments made by office check.
